{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZZ0rmw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDBI6A", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 75, "title": "Add an evidence-qualified Telecon BiZ database retrieval journey from MAIN 4", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `3ca886667c6dc30144c9941c04608d70ab76ed62`, source inspection shows that MAIN `4 データベース` opens `データベース一覧：0件`. `LIST` repeats the empty collection, and retrieval commands are rejected. Users cannot experience database selection, searching, title inspection or article retrieval.

This advances the intentional placeholder scope of [Issue #33](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/33). It is a remaining fidelity gap, not a regression introduced by the latest pacing correction.

## Expected outcome

Provide one keyboard-operated, browser-local journey:

`MAIN → 4 データベース → database directory → 日経テレコン BiZ → keyword search → numbered result set and count → titles → full article → return`

Directory selector `1` opens BiZ. Inside that destination, support the small normalized subset `FIND keyword`, `SHOW P1 /n` and `SHOW P3 /n item`. Item numbers refer to positions within the specified result set.

Bundle four short, original Japanese example articles appropriate to late 1996. Include overlapping and distinct search terms so multiple-result, single-result and no-result searches work. Do not attribute invented prose to an actual newspaper or present it as recovered reporting.

## Context

Historical sources inspected on 2026-10-23:

- The [NEC PC-VAN office article](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jkg/43/3/43_KJ00002959297/_pdf/-char/ja), March 1993, identifies the BiZ gateway and newspaper-article retrieval. High confidence within its earlier-year scope; it supplies no complete 1996 gateway session.
- The [March 1995 development report](https://www.jipdec.or.jp/archives/publications/J0000844.pdf) identifies BiZ as its target. Printed pages 64–67 describe transmitted FIND searches, numbered sets, P1 title output and P3 content selection. Page 64 specifies half-width blanks between syntax-table fields. Confidence is high in these documented semantics; OCR compresses examples and both page-image requests failed. Its Windows dialogs and connection automation are client behavior, not host screens.
- The [participant chronology](https://www.infosta.or.jp/journal/rensai05.pdf), August 2008, dates PC-VAN gateway connection to November 1992, Telecon21 introduction to January 1997 and BiZ retirement to December 1999. Moderate confidence for retrospective chronology; this does not prove command continuity.
- The [March 1997 clearing-server report](https://www.jipdec.or.jp/archives/publications/J0000907.pdf), printed pages 22–23, dates its command information to August 1996 and references RUKIT's October 1996 retrieval manual. This is a useful follow-up lead, not an inspected BiZ command specification. An accessible [April 1997 recommendation](https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jkg/47/4/47_KJ00002307006/_pdf/-char/ja), printed page 204, independently identifies that manual; the manual itself remains uninspected.

**Accepted reconstruction:** carry this earlier documented command subset into the November 1996 setting. Continuity confidence is moderate, not authenticated. MAIN 4 placement, directory selector, prompts, layouts, normalized command spacing, matching rules, result-set limits and return controls are authored reconstruction. Exact gateway entry/exit and target-year error wording remain unknown. Do not import Telecon21's later web interface or another provider's commands.

Implementation boundaries:

- `src/sections.ts` defines the empty database collection; `src/navigation.ts` owns screen state and parent returns.
- `src/eic.ts`, `src/service-collections.ts` and `tests/eic.spec.ts` provide suitable static-content, literal-rendering and service-isolation patterns. Reuse these conventions without introducing a generic service framework.
- `src/commands.ts` dispatches composition, mail and OLT separately. Database views must expose none of those contexts.
- `tests/sections.spec.ts` and `tests/navigation.spec.ts` currently require MAIN 4 to remain empty. Replace those specific obsolete expectations while retaining every other destination check.
- Live repository searches found no open Issues or PRs. Related completed scopes include [immersive presentation #31](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/31), [library/OSL #59](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/59) and [EIC readings #69](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/69); none implements BiZ retrieval.
- [PR #74](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/74) and `docs/validation.md` record 259 passing checks, including configured type checking and production build. These are Coordinator-reported results; this research graph ran no application validation.

Scope is this single database journey. News, other providers, Boolean/set-combination expressions, date/media filters, remote connections, credentials, billing and storage migrations remain outside scope.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] MAIN 4 opens a concise database directory. Selecting `1` opens a separately identified BiZ search view with working command examples. Access requires no handle, AI or external connection. Preserve the existing MAIN fixture's label and selector; do not invent a historical jump keyword.
- [ ] Implement one whitespace-free keyword per FIND request, using documented literal substring matching over bundled titles and bodies. Command words are case-insensitive; preserve the entered keyword for display and use case-insensitive Latin matching. Unsupported expressions receive contextual guidance rather than silently behaving as a full query language.
- [ ] Successful searches create stable visit-local sets `/1`, `/2`, and so on, displaying the query and hit count. Existing sets retain their article order and meaning after later searches. A zero-hit search reports zero and creates no set. Retain at most 20 successful sets per visit; at capacity, preserve existing sets and explain how to leave and re-enter. These lifecycle choices are disclosed reconstruction, not historical limits.
- [ ] `SHOW P1 /n` lists the specified set's numbered titles. `SHOW P3 /n item` displays the corresponding complete article. Reject absent sets, malformed syntax, zero/negative/fractional/unsafe numbers, out-of-range items and trailing arguments without changing existing sets or the active view. FIND/SHOW remain scoped to BiZ.
- [ ] `HELP` redisplays the current view without changing results. `BACK` follows article → that set's titles → search/results → database directory → actual entry parent, including `2 索引 → 4`. `MAIN` clears the nested path. Repeated FIND/SHOW commands replace the appropriate active view without accumulating duplicate parents. Leaving BiZ clears its transient sets; re-entry starts fresh. Separate controller instances cannot share results.
- [ ] Include four original, undated Japanese example articles with deterministic ordering. Source material is used only for structural evidence: no copied archived articles, identities, images or software. Bundled records and search results remain outside IndexedDB and backups. Browsing cannot repopulate empty boards or alter members, SIGs, forums, posts, mail, read markers, conference/OLT records, consent or historical-calendar settings. Existing session/history bookkeeping continues normally.
- [ ] Database screens expose no forum destination, mailbox, conference or OLT participation context. Composition, reply and room commands cannot create records there. Preserve global application shortcuts and Settings/About return behavior. Continue rendering content and queries as literal text through the existing terminal renderer.
- [ ] Update README usage/destination descriptions, `docs/research/pcvan-1996-1997.md` and existing About/Details content. Record source URLs, inspection dates, historical scope, confidence, failed page-image access and the distinction between documented command semantics and reconstructed behavior. Keep routine terminal output concise Japanese with provenance available on demand.
- [ ] Extend existing controller and Playwright coverage for zero/single/multiple matches, every article, retained earlier sets, repeated queries, the set limit, invalid syntax/numbers, service isolation, direct/index parents, MAIN from each depth and fresh re-entry. Include production-browser journeys with and without a handle, a Japanese IME-confirmation check for FIND input, Settings/About return, literal markup, 320px scrolling and terminal-log inclusion. Using existing snapshot helpers with automatic activity paused, verify protected records remain unchanged, including restored empty worlds; allow normal session/history changes. Verify browsing introduces no remote requests.
- [ ] Preserve existing functional, storage/import/reset, consent, composition, mail/OLT, calendar, IME and terminal pacing/skip regression coverage. The Coordinator runs documented `npm test` before merge; Playwright's configured servers already perform TypeScript checking and production build. Review the final diff, check Markdown/local links and run `git diff --check`. Record actual commands, results and any failures. No new framework, real inference or model download is needed.

## Optional validation

An accessible copy of the October 1996 RUKIT manual or a dated BiZ gateway session could refine command spacing and entry/exit behavior. Further research and visual comparison are optional refinements, not completion gates. No human confirmation or historical hardware check is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance checks are achievable before merge.
